standard.title: Perform with technical skills
standard.description: practise and perform dances using technical and expressive skills in informal and/or formal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can practise and perform dances in informal settings (Y3-4). They use expressive skills (projection, focus) and can communicate intent to an audience and reflect on performance.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students practise and perform dances using technical and expressive skills in informal and/or formal settings.

nodes.label: Technical and expressive skill in rehearsal
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply technical and expressive skills in rehearsal — working within their body capabilities and improving quality across multiple attempts.
nodes.minimum_width: Rehearsing a dance with awareness of technical skill application (e.g. landing alignment, balance) and at least one expressive skill — able to identify what they are working to improve.
nodes.typical_width: Rehearsing learned and/or self-choreographed dances with awareness of body capabilities; applying technical and expressive skills; creating tension through slow controlled movements with neutral facial expression; using Viewpoints questions to reflect on spatial placement, focus, musicality, clarity.
wider: Use video to review rehearsal — identifying specific technical and expressive skill development areas and setting targeted goals
Rehearse across multiple sessions with a documented improvement focus — tracking change in a performance journal or checklist

response_modes.reason: Rehearsal skill — the capacity to use repetition productively and target improvements — is itself a learnable practice. Students benefit from explicit rehearsal strategy instruction alongside content.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who develop deliberate rehearsal habits and reflective practice tools at this level enter Y7-8 with the self-directed learning capacity to develop genre-specific techniques independently.
success_criteria: Student can identify at least one technical and one expressive skill they are working on in rehearsal
Student shows improvement in a target skill across multiple rehearsal sessions

nodes.label: Performing for audiences in varied settings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform dances in informal and/or formal settings — using technical and expressive skills and appropriate production elements to communicate ideas to an audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Performing one dance in an informal or formal setting using at least two technical-expressive skills; using at least one production element where appropriate.
nodes.typical_width: Performing in informal and/or formal settings: using specific technical and expressive skills to communicate ideas, perspectives or meaning; using production elements (music, costumes, props) to enhance different contexts; performing with cultural community representatives using traditional music where appropriate; using Viewpoints questions to reflect on performance.
wider: Perform a dance for an audience beyond the class — a school assembly, community event, or online platform — adapting performance presence for the context
Perform a dance using traditional music when presenting with representatives of the cultural group from the community — following relevant cultural protocols
nodes.hinge_reason: Performance in varied settings — including formal contexts — is the experiential foundation for the more demanding performance requirements of Y7-8. Students who have only ever performed in highly informal single-class settings lack the performance confidence and audience awareness that formal contexts require.

response_modes.reason: Performance integrates rehearsal skill (N1), technical-expressive skill, and production element choices into a communicative event. The audience relationship is the critical new element at this node — frame performance as communication, not demonstration.

success_criteria: Student performs a dance using at least two identifiable technical-expressive skills
Student can use at least one production element purposefully in performance
Student can reflect on their performance using a Viewpoints question — identifying one strength and one area for development
